prompt: Implement CheckerPainter.paint to draw a cells-by-cells checkerboard: each square is cellSize pixels, BLACK where (row + col) is even, WHITE otherwise.
explanation: Grid drawings almost always come from two nested loops: the outer over rows, the inner over columns, converting grid coordinates to pixels by multiplying by the cell size (columns map to x, rows to y). The (row + col) % 2 parity test is the classic trick for alternating colors, because moving one step in any direction flips the parity. Each iteration sets a color and fills exactly one square.
hints: Loop row from 0 to cells - 1, and inside it loop col the same way.
(row + col) % 2 == 0 tells you whether the square is black.
The square's pixel position is fillRect(col * cellSize, row * cellSize, cellSize, cellSize).
